modules.content:
## Recommended System Requirements for Editor 14

### Recommended Requirements

Synergy recommends the following specifications for running Editor 14 with local capture and advanced editing workflows.

#### Mac

- macOS 12.0 Monterey or later
- Intel quad-core i5 processor or better and quad-core or greater
  - At least 2.3 GHz before Turbo Boost
  - M1 processors are supported
- 8 GB RAM, 16 GB is recommended
- 512 GB or greater hard disk storage, 1 TB is recommended
- Discrete graphics card
- Display resolution 1280 x 800 or better

#### Windows

- Windows 10 (64-bit)
- Intel quad-core i5 processor or better and quad-core or greater
  - At least 2.3 GHz before Turbo Boost
  - ARM processors are not supported, i.e. some editions of MS Surface
- 8 GB RAM, 16 GB is recommended
- 512 GB or greater hard disk storage, 1 TB is recommended
- Discrete graphics card
- Display resolution 1024 x 768 or better

> NOTE: Multi-core i5 devices that meet the requirements above will support basic playlist viewing and sharing but, but might experience performance downgrades accessing more dynamic workflows.

### Connectivity

- 15 MBPS download speed
  - Bandwidth may be checked [here](https://www.speedtest.net/)
- -60dBm signal strength or better (closer to zero)
  - Signal strength may be checked [here](https://www.howtogeek.com/426642/how-to-check-your-wi-fi-signal-strength/)

####

### Recording Hardware

- AJA U-TAP updated with the [latest](https://www.aja.com/support) firmware. The links below each include distinct downloads for PC and Mac
  - [HDMI](https://www.aja.com/products/u-tap-hdmi#support)
  - [SDI](https://www.aja.com/products/u-tap-sdi#support)

If you need any assistance updating your operating system or have any other questions related to Synergy applications, please don't hesitate to reach out to our Support Team via email at [support@synergysports.com](mailto:support@synergysportstech.com) or by phone at 1-800-411-1627.

## Getting Started with Editor 14

### Welcome

Synergy Sports is excited to introduce Synergy Editor 14! Designed to provide you with a best-in-industry user experience integrated into the Synergy environment, the Synergy Editor 14 retains and refines all of the features that make the Editor unique while adding many new features to ease the workflow and provide an unparalleled experience.

### Overview

The Synergy Editor 14 delivers several exciting new features: new practice workflows including the ability to publish user tagged practice data to the Synergy Team Site, printable box scores directly from the Editor, improved Matrix view, new right-click menus for easier maneuverability within the app, and more.

###

### Compare Synergy Base Editor and Synergy Editor Max

![Screenshot: Getting Started with Editor 14](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565509-01.png)

###

### Recommended Requirements

To view the Synergy Editor 14's recommended requirements, click here. (see the “Setting Up Editor 14” lesson)

### Getting Started

#### Installing Synergy Editor 14

Use the links below to install the Synergy Editor 14 application:

- Basketball: <https://www.synergysportstech.com/apps/editor/basketball>
- Baseball: <https://www.synergysportstech.com/apps/editor/baseball>
- Softball: <https://www.synergysportstech.com/apps/editor/softball>

**For PC**: Select Download (Intel)

**For MAC**: Select Download (Silicon)

![Screenshot: Getting Started with Editor 14](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565509-02.jpg)

**For PC**: Once downloaded, run the application and complete any installation prompts.

**For Mac**: Once downloaded, move the Synergy Editor 14 from the Downloads to the Application folder as seen here:

![Screenshot: Getting Started with Editor 14](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565509-03.gif)

> Note: Silicon is the best performing build, but it is not compatible with older Macs. If you are not able to drag the Editor into Applications, please download the Intel version, which works on all Macs.

Lastly, navigate to your Applications and launch Editor 14.

**Ensure the following:**

- Synergy files are written to the Documents folder on your computer's hard drive (not cloud or networked drives, which often have limitations).
- The Documents folder should have at least 25 GB of available disk space.
- You must also have Read/Write permissions on the specified Documents folder.

For questions, support, or feedback, feel free to reach out to our Support Team via email at [support@synergysports.com](mailto:support@synergysportstech.com) or by phone, any time, at 1-800-411-1627.

## Importing Sportscode

### **Import the Edits Video**

Locate the video file on your local machine, then drag and drop the file directly into the Synergy Editor application. An Import Videopopup will appear.

- Ensure the dropdown is set to **Create Timeline**.
- Name your edit (the edit name will default to the file name).
- Click **OK** to begin the import.

![Screenshot: Importing Sportscode](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000596228-01.jpg)

### **Import Clips XML**

Once the video has finished importing and the edit is open, click the **three-line menu** (hamburger menu) located at the top-left corner of the edit window. Select **Import Clips XML...** from the dropdown menu.

![Screenshot: Importing Sportscode](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000596228-02.jpg)

A file explorer window will open. Select your desired .xml file and click **Open**.

![Screenshot: Importing Sportscode](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000596228-03.jpg)

### **Finalize**

The Editor will display an "Importing edit from XML" status bar. Once complete, the clips will be automatically placed on the timeline above your video.

![Screenshot: Importing Sportscode](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000596228-04.jpg)

## Presentation Remote Compatibility

#### **Overview**

Synergy Editor supports wireless presentation remotes, giving coaches and staff hands-free video control during film sessions and team meetings.

#### **Hardware Compatibility****Optimized for****Logitech R400 Wireless Presenter**

#### (USB-A, list price: $39.99). We strongly recommend having your program or organization purchase one for your film room setup.

![Screenshot: Presentation Remote Compatibility](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000598941-01.png)

#### **Controls**

| **Remote Button** | **Gesture** | **Default Action** | **Function Details** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Laser** | **Single Tap** | **Laser Pointer** | Flashes the physical red laser beam. |
|  | **Press & Hold** *(>0.3s)* | **Laser Pointer** | Fires the physical red laser beam. |
| **Left (****◀ )** Page Up | **Single Tap** | **Previous Clip** | Skips to the beginning of the previous clip. |
|  | **Press & Hold** *(>0.3s)* | **Rewind (REW)** | Rewinds video at **2x speed** while held. This increases to **3x speed** if held for 2.5 seconds.  Release to resume. |
| **Right (****▶ )** Page Down | **Single Tap** | **Next Clip** | Advances to the next clip in the playlist. |
|  | **Press & Hold** *(>0.3s)* | **Fast Forward (FF)** | Advances video at **2x speed** while held. This increases to **3x speed** if held for 2.5 seconds. Release to resume. |
| **Slideshow** F5 / Esc | **Single Tap** | **Full Screen / Windowed** | Toggles presentation full-screen mode *(press again if cycling between states)*. |
| **Black Screen****.** (Period) | **Single Tap** | **Play / Pause** | Toggles playback instantly with zero delay. |

#### **Activating & Customizing Your Hotkeys**

##### **Reset Hotkeys After Updating (Required)**

To enable remote compatibility after downloading the updated Editor, you must reset your hotkey profile to load the new defaults:

1. Open the **Hotkeys** menu in Synergy Editor.
2. Select **Reset**

**Note***:* If you previously configured custom keyboard shortcuts, resetting will clear them. Re-enter your personal hotkeys after performing the reset. You can cancel the hotkey reset instead of confirming if you need to note your previous hotkey assignments.

![Screenshot: Presentation Remote Compatibility](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000598941-02.jpg)

##### **Customizing Button Mappings**

You can remap remote buttons to any action you prefer in the **Hotkeys** menu. While the default profile has multiple function buttons using tap vs. hold gestures, custom assignments through the Hotkeys UI currently support one function per button. If you reassign a remote button manually, it will execute only that single assigned action.

##### **Quick Setup**

1. **Plug & Play:** Insert the USB-A receiver into your computer and turn the remote power switch to **ON**.
2. **Focus the Editor:** Click anywhere inside the Editor video window to ensure it has active keyboard focus.
3. **Scrubbing vs. Skipping:** Tap the directional buttons for **Previous/Next Clip**; hold for more than **0.3 seconds** for **2x Rewind/Fast Forward**. After holding for **2.5 seconds**, it increases to **3x speed**.

#### **Other Remotes**

Many other presentation remotes work as well. Because button layouts and keystrokes vary, other models simply require mapping your preferred functions in the Hotkeys menu. Contact Synergy Support if you have questions about specific third-party devices.

## Cowboy Remote

### Overview

You can use the remote to control video only in the Editor. The Remote does not work with the Silverlight Player in your browser.

### Button Breakdown

![Screenshot: Cowboy Remote](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565646-01.jpg)

### Compatibility

The 14 Button Cowboy Remote works with both PC and Mac versions of the Synergy Editor and Max Editor. It also works with both local capture and Synergy clips. Unlike previous versions of the app, Mac users do not need to run Source Manager at the same time as the Editor or Max Editor.

## MAX: Importing Video

### Overview

The Synergy Editor Max allows you to import your own previously recorded video directly into the Synergy Editor using the Source Manager integration. This convenient and essential feature allows you to breakdown footage of practices, exhibition games, and more while keeping your workflow streamlined and efficient.

### Getting Started

To begin, click the **Import Video** icon, located at the top-right of the Editor, or click the **+** icon in the bottom right of any open panel, and select **Import Video**from the menu.

![Screenshot: MAX: Importing Video](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565522-01.jpg)

The Import Video window will pop-up, allowing you to set up the parameters of your import. Start by browsing for the file(s) by clicking the three dots to the right of the **File** text box. Select the file(s) you'd like to import. Once selected, you can preview the files prior to import by selecting the file from the dropdown above the preview window, and clicking the play button. This helps ensure you have selected the correct video file(s) to be imported.

Once you've ensured the correct video files have been selected, you can set the Date of the event, set the Event Type, and title the video you're uploading by using the **Edit Name** text box.

Click the**Create Edit** checkbox if you would like the Editor to create a new Custom Edit of the import automatically.

You have a couple of options to choose from as to how the video files will be imported:

- **Express** - This option enables immediate full access to your video. The video may later be pushed to the Synergy Cloud from the Videos tab to enable sharing with other users.
- **Push to Synergy Cloud** - This option will push your video to the Synergy Cloud, making it available to all users on your team's account.
- **Include Audio** - Choose whether or not to include the audio with your imported file(s).

When all of your selections have been made, click the **OK** button to begin the import process. If the Create Edit checkbox was selected, the video will appear automatically in a timeline in the lower panel of the Editor. If the checkbox was not selected, the file(s) will be available in the Videos tab at the top of the application.

![Screenshot: MAX: Importing Video](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565522-02.jpg)

> NOTE: A line will appear above the timeline of your import. A green line indicates the video is only available locally. A blue line indicates it has been pushed to the Synergy Cloud. Details of the asset are listed under the Videos Tab, and local files can be pushed to the cloud from here.

## Sending Video to the Editor from Team Site

### Overview

Utilizing video from the Synergy Team Site in the Editor is one of the foundational processes of the application. Being able to curate your own custom playlists from Synergy tagged clips allows you to focus on what is important to you and your team and produce professional playlists that meet your needs.

### Video Default Settings

Before sending video from the Synergy Team Site to the Editor, it's recommended to set your Video Default Settings. You can choose the Editor as your default playback and destination from the Settings on the Team Site, or opt to be asked which destination you'd prefer (the In-browser player or Editor) each time you select clips. Start by selecting **Settings** from the User Menu on the Team Site. In the Video Default Settings section, use the switches and drop-downs to set your default playback selections. Once your selections have been made, click **Save Changes** to apply the settings.

- **Video Playback Options**
  - Send Video Straight to Default
  - Ask Video Preference Every Time
- **Playback**
  - In-Browser Player
  - Editor
- **Max Clips**
  - 25
  - 50
  - 100
  - 250
  - 500
  - 800
  - 1000
- **Clip Order**
  - Most Recent First
  - Oldest First
  - Random Order
- **Video Quality**
  - Standard Quality
  - High Quality

### Sending Video to the Editor

As you navigate through the Team Site, any statistic listed in blue indicates there is associated video. Click the stat to engage your playback choices. If you selected *Ask Video Preferences Every Time*from the settings, a pop-up window will open, and you can revise your default choices. Ensure Editor is set as the playback destination. Click **OK** and a temporary playlist will open in the Editor.

![Screenshot: Sending Video to the Editor from Team Site](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565510-01.jpg)

Once in the Editor, you can choose to save the temporary playlist as a Custom Edit, export it, or a number of other options by using the carrot menu on the edit's tab. You can also drag and drop individual clips from the temporary edit into other existing edits or use the hotkeys to send active clips to your Destination edit.

![Screenshot: Sending Video to the Editor from Team Site](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565510-02.jpg)

> NOTE: If not saved, temporary edits will be removed when the Editor is closed. Temporary playlists are identifiable by the italicized title with an * before the name.

## Synergy Source Manager

### Overview

The Synergy Source Manager can be used to import or capture video (but it is not necessary after updating to Synergy Editor 10 or later). It is also needed for users who intend on importing a Sportscode package into your Synergy Editor for use.

#### Installing the Synergy Source Manager

Use the link below to install the Synergy Source Manager application:

<https://www.synergysportstech.com/apps/sourcemanager/production>

**For PC**: Once downloaded, run the application and complete any installation prompts.

**For Mac**: Once downloaded, move the Synergy Source Manager from the Downloads to the Application folder in the same manner as seen above.

Lastly, navigate to your Applications and launch the Source Manager.

### Documents Folder Setup

It is important to ensure that associated folders for both the Editor and the Source Manager are located in the same place on your computer. Once the applications are installed, Ensure that a Synergy Sports folder has been created in your LOCAL documents folder and contains an additional folder both for the Editor and the Source manager.

**Note:**The individual application folders may not appear until you have opened/utilized the applications

**Ensure the following:**

- Synergy files are written to the Documents folder on your computer’s hard drive (not cloud or networked drives, which often have limitations).
- The Documents folder should be at least 25 GB of available disk space.
- You must also have Read/Write permissions on the specified Documents folder.

If you install the applications and the Synergy Sports folder is not present in your local Documents folder, please contact our Support Team ([support@synergysports.com](mailto:support@synergysports.com)) for assistance.

### Getting Started

Click the app icon to launch the Synergy Source Manager and log in using your Synergy credentials.

![Screenshot: Synergy Source Manager](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565639-01.jpg)

If you log in and receive this message, you do not need to work directly with this application.

![Screenshot: Synergy Source Manager](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565639-02.jpg)

### Capture

The application defaults to the Capture tab. Use the designated fields to set up the capture before starting. The Name field defaults to the current date and time. To change this, click in the **Name** text box and enter your desired name. Change the Date by typing in the associated text box or by using the arrows to the right to increase or decrease the date. Label your event by using the **Event Type** drop-down menu. Choose from *Other, Practice, Exhibition,*or *Game.*In the Video drop-down menu, select your input device or select **RTMP Stream**if you will be using SACS cameras. Make a similar selection in the Audio drop-down to select your connected audio devices.

Check the **Push to Synergy Cloud**box to automatically upload your capture to the Synergy Cloud for easy sharing or to make it accessible to the rest of your team or staff.

Check **Display Live Preview** to preview the camera video as it is captured.

*
![Screenshot: Synergy Source Manager](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565639-03.jpg)*

Once you are ready to begin, click **Start Capture** to begin capturing your video for use with the Synergy Editor.

### Import

In the Source Manager, select the **Import** tab to upload existing video for use with the Synergy Editor. Select your **Import Type**from the drop-down menu, along with the **Name**, **Date**, and **Event Type** as you would with a capture. Use the ellipsis button to the right of the File text box in the Source section to browse your computer or device for the file you would like to import.

Check the **Push to Synergy Cloud**box to automatically upload your capture to the Synergy Cloud for easy sharing or to make it accessible to the rest of your team or staff.

![Screenshot: Synergy Source Manager](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565639-04.jpg)

Once you are ready to begin, click **Start Import** to begin importing your video for use with the Synergy Editor.

### Video Manager

Imported video assets are managed via the Video Manager tab. Click to view a list of all your imports. Click **Refresh** in the upper left to refresh the whole list. Click to check the box next to **Available Only** to view assets that have completed the import process.

View the details of an import by clicking on the name in the row. This expands the options available.  Choose to *Refresh*, *Download/Upload*, *Delete Local*, *Add/Remove Game*, and *Create Edit.*

- Refresh: refresh an import in the event it is disrupted
- Download: download an import to your local machine
- Upload: upload an import to the cloud
- Delete Local: remove a file that you downloaded to your computer
- Add Game:  add an import to an existing game
- Remove Game: remove the import's association to an existing game
- Create Edit: opens the import in the Synergy Editor, ready to to be clipped and added to a Custom Edit

When selecting **Add/Remove Game,** a new window opens. Select the details from the drop-down menus at the top to populate your game schedule, then select the game you would like to add the import to.

![Screenshot: Synergy Source Manager](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565639-05.jpg)

### Summary

The Synergy Source Manager offers an additional option when looking to import or capture your own video for use with the Synergy Editor. With a straightforward interface, starting an upload or import is simple and convenient.

## MAX: Starting a Live Capture

### Overview

Live Capture is a vital tool within the Synergy Editor Max. This feature allows you to capture your practice, games, and more, directly into the Editor for immediate review, scouting, or teaching purposes.

### Getting Started

Setting up your camera hardware is an important first step. If you are using a stand-alone camera to capture your video, please follow the instructions listed for the AJA U-TAP Capture Device. (see the “Live Capture and Streaming” lesson)Once you have your devices set up, you are ready to start a live capture. To initiate a live capture from the Editor, select the **New Live Capture** button from the top right of the application, or select the **+** icon from the bottom right of any open panel and select **New Live Capture** from the menu.

![Screenshot: MAX: Starting a Live Capture](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565636-01.jpg)

The New Live Capture window will appear, giving you options to input:

- There is a checkbox to **Create Edit**, this will automatically create a custom edit within the Editor where your live capture will save to during the capture. If you select this, you also are able to give your set your **Edit Name** in the associated text box.
- Change the **File Name** to something distinct for future reference, as the video file for your capture will be saved under the Videos tab at the top of the application with the file name as the title.
- Set your **Event Type** to Game, Exhibition, Practice, or Other.
- Select your **Video** input. When using a stand-alone camera, connect through the AJA U-TAP device. To live capture through the Synergy Automated Camera System, or connect to a different RTMP stream, follow the instructions listed here.
- Select your **Audio** input if available.
- **Push to Synergy Cloud**, making the video available to all users on your team's account as it is captured.
- **Performance Mode** creates a 15 second delay, allowing for a more fluid live viewing if you are experiencing poor connectivity or you are recording to an device with lesser performance.

![Screenshot: MAX: Starting a Live Capture](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565636-02.jpg)

Initiating a live capture can also be started by selecting the **Start/Stop Capture** button located above the timeline view. This will open the same capture window described above. Input the requested information and click **OK** to start your capture.

![Screenshot: MAX: Starting a Live Capture](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565636-03.jpg)

## Live Capture: AJA Capture Device

### Overview

The Synergy Editor 11 includes support for a new video capture device that simplifies the capture process from your camera or other video sources. The live capture workflow requires the use of an AJA U-TAP capture device.

![Screenshot: Live Capture: AJA Capture Device](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565638-01.jpg)
![Screenshot: Live Capture: AJA Capture Device](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565638-02.jpg)

The AJA-UTAP comes in both an HDMI version and an SDI version.

The AJA-UTAP supports the following:

- Capturing video via an HDMI chord (HDMI model)
- Capturing video via an SDI chord (SDI model)
- USB 3.0 connection to a desktop or laptop computer

### Setting Up and Understanding the AJA U-TAP

**HDMI VERSION:**

**Status LED**

- Off = not connected
- Red = USB connected to a USB 2.0 port
- Green = USB connected to a USB 3.0 port
- Blinking = U-TAP is streaming video, audio, or both power

**LED**

- Off = no power
- Green = power present

**U-TAP HDMI LOCK LED**

- Off = not locked to source video
- Green = locked to SD video source
- Red = locked to an HD video source

**SDI VERSION**

**Status LED**

- Off = not connected
- Red = USB connected to a USB 2.0 port
- Green = USB connected to a USB 3.0 port
- Blinking = U-TAP is streaming video, audio, or both power

**LED**

- Off = no power
- Green = power present

**U-TAP SDI LOCK LED**

- Off = not locked to source video
- Green = locked to 270Mbps source
- Red = locked to 1.5Gbps video source
- Amber = locked to 3Gbps video source

#### System Connection

![Screenshot: Live Capture: AJA Capture Device](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565638-03.jpg)

Connecting to the AJA U-TAP device is very simple and requires no additional software. View the diagram above for how to connect the device. Be sure to use any included cords that come with the device to ensure a good connection.

### Where to Purchase

The AJA-UTAP can be purchased from several retailers, including:

- B&H Photo
  - [HDMI Version](https://www.bhphotovideo.com/c/product/1248099-REG/aja_u_tap_hdmi_u_tap_usb_3_0_powered.html)
  - [SDI Version](https://www.bhphotovideo.com/c/product/1248098-REG/aja_u_tap_sdi_u_tap_usb_3_0_powered.html)
- Newegg
  - [HDMI Version](https://www.newegg.com/p/2CX-0010-00025?Description=aja%20utap&cm_re=aja_utap-_-9SIAEPZ7CB9494-_-Product&quicklink=true)
  - [SDI Version](https://www.newegg.com/p/2CX-0010-00024?Description=aja%20utap&cm_re=aja_utap-_-2CX-0010-00024-_-Product&quicklink=true)

They can also be found at other retailers; if you purchase from another retailer please be sure the device matches the products linked above.

If you need to convert from SDI to HDMI or HDMI to SDI to support your setup, several adapters are available:

- [SDI to HDMI Converter](https://www.bhphotovideo.com/c/product/1247784-REG/blackmagic_design_convcmic_sh_micro_converter_sdi_to.html)
- [HDMI to SDI Converter](https://www.bhphotovideo.com/c/product/1247783-REG/blackmagic_design_convcmic_hs_micro_converter_hdmi_to.html)

­If you require assistance using the AJA device with Synergy Editor 11 please feel free to contact our Support Team at any time by phone 1-800-411-1627, or by email at support@synergysports.com

## MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor

### Overview

Using Sportshub, you can now wirelessly stream your scheduled SACS recordings directly into the Synergy Editor Max from anywhere in the world. Whether courtside or in your office, this simple process allows for easy live capture for you to tag your games and practices in real time.

#### Getting Started

To get started, click the **Camera** tab above the upper right panel, next to the Videos tab. Then click the red **Connect Account** button. This will take you to the Keemotion page.

![Screenshot: MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565637-01.jpg)

Enter your SACS credentials to log in.

![Screenshot: MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565637-02.jpg)

> Note: If you wish to change the SACS account you are using, select the **Reconnect Camera** option from the File menu.

You will be asked to share your data with Synergy Client App. Confirm your connection by clicking **Accept**.

![Screenshot: MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565637-03.jpg)

Once you are connected, Division I users will see their own scheduled games and practices, as well as games from other Division I Teams. All other Max users will see only their own events.

The **MyArena Schedule/Edit** button in the upper right corner, connects you to the Keemotion site scheduling page.

![Screenshot: MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565637-04.jpg)

> Note: Newly scheduled events will be seen in the Editor following a refresh of the application.

![Screenshot: MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565637-05.jpg)

Once events are scheduled for recording by Keemotion, they must be scheduled for ingestion by Synergy to make them compatible for adding to your Edits. To request an ingestion, simply **right click** on the event, and select **Schedule Ingestion**.

If the event occurred in the past, the ingestion will begin immediately.

![Screenshot: MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565637-06.jpg)

To request an automatic ingestion for a future event, use the toggle above your list of events to select Upcoming/Live, and then right click on the event, and select Schedule Ingestion. This will begin the ingestion automatically once the recording has begun.

![Screenshot: MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565637-07.jpg)

These video assets may be attached to Edits just as a video from the Videos panel would. To create a new edit with your recording, select the recording and click the **+** icon in the upper right, or right click on the recording and select **Create Edit**.

A dialog box will appear, allowing you to choose between creating a **Timeline** or **Custom Edit**, **Name** your edit, and select which **Panel** you would like to open it in. Once you have made your selections click **OK**.

![Screenshot: MAX: Wireless Streaming Your Synergy Camera in the Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565637-08.jpg)

> Note: It can take up to two minutes from when the encoding is requested, or when an event starts, until it is available in an Edit. Once the encoding is complete, it will look just like a regular Timeline, and will start caching the video.

modules.content:
## Overview

The timeline is a dynamic, information-rich view in the Synergy Editor. Timeline view is available for imported or captured video, as well as full game edits downloaded from the Synergy Team Site, allowing you to do more with your video than ever before. With dynamic and improved tagging and more detailed and useful filters and tools, timeline view offer an excellent way to visualize and break down your film for a variety of uses.

### Full Game Edits

Full game edits can be downloaded from the Synergy Team Site and reviewed using the timeline view. Using the Game tab on the Team Site, select **Full Game Video** and assure the playback is set to **Editor**.

A timeline of the full game edit will automatically populate the lower left panel of the Editor, displaying a visualization of all of the Synergy clips in chronological order organized in data specific, expandable rows on the left side of the Timeline. Any clip or row can be viewed by simply double-clicking.

> NOTE: Full game edits are sent to the Editor as a temporary edit, indicated with an asterisk and italicized title as shown above. The timeline will be removed from the Editor when the application is closed, unless the edit is saved by selecting the **carrot icon** on the edit tab and selecting **Save**.

### Autoplay Toggle

With the Autoplay toggle, you can choose to either view your playlist or timeline one clip at a time, or allow the clips to play continuously. Click the Autoplay toggle to turn on or off.

![Screenshot: Timeline View](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565516-01.jpg)

Toggle Autoplay on, and your video will automatically begin the next clip as soon as your previous clip has finished, without having to watch repeat footage from overlapping clips.

![Screenshot: Timeline View](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565516-02.jpg)

Toggle Autoplay off, and each clip will play from beginning to end, and pause at the end of your clip. You will then need to manually select and start the next clip you would like to watch.

![Screenshot: Timeline View](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565516-03.jpg)

### Right-Click Menus

Right-clicking on any data row will bring up a menu of options including:

- **Flag Row** - Marks a row with a customizable color for easy filtering and sharing data of particular interest with your staff
- **Hide Row** - Hides a row and the clips within to help with visual clutter. The row can be restored by clicking between the row numbers where previously displayed
- **Save Row as Custom Edit** - Automatically creates a Custom Edit of all clips within the selected data row
- **Export** - Exports all clips within the selected data row for offline viewing or sharing via flash drive
- **Delete** - Deletes all clips within the selected row. A pop-up window will appear to confirm your selection in order to prevent accidental deletion

Right-clicking any clip within the timeline will bring up a menu of options including:

- **Add User Tags*** - Add your own additional tags to the Synergy tags if desired
- **Open Hierarchy*** - Opens the tagging hierarchy to help select additional Synergy tags, or create new user tags
- **Export** - Exports all clips within the selected data row for offline viewing or sharing via flash drive
- **Delete** - Deletes all clips within the selected row. A pop-up window will appear to confirm your selection in order to prevent accidental deletion

> *NOTE: Tagging video features are exclusively available to Editor Max users.

### Timeline Toolbar

![Screenshot: Timeline View](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565516-04.jpg)

Across the top of the Timeline, you can access the following items from left to right:

- **Classic/Players/Team/User Tags Only Perspective**
  - Classic Perspective will display all tagged events on the timeline
  - Players Perspective will display a breakdown of all events by player, including stats, outcomes, play types, and user tags
  - Team Perspective will display the selected team's tagged events grouped by Offense and Defense. This perspective is only available on Synergy created Timelines, not local capture or imports
  - User Tags Only Perspective will display only User tags, and hide all of the Synergy Tagged data. This is particularly useful if you would like to start with a blank timeline of Full Game footage imported from the Synergy Team Site.
- **Start/Stop Capture***
  - Create a new live capture, or append a new capture on top of an existing local capture
- **Jump To Live***
  - Automatically jump to the video that is currently being captured live
- **Magnifier**
  - Zoom in and out of the Timeline using the slider
- **Filter**
  - Filter the Timeline to only display the rows desired e.g. Team, Player, Event Type, and Flagged Clips
- **Tag Owner**
  - Filter the Timeline to only display the tags created by Synergy, yourself, or another member of your staff
- **Column Text Overlay**
  - Select a data column to be displayed as text in the video player for the selected clip
- **Follow Play Head**
  - Keeps the play head in the center of the Timeline at all times, scrolling the Timeline horizontally to stay present with the video being played
- **Flag Clips**
  - Marks a clip or set of clips allowing for easy filtering and sharing clips of particular interest with the staff
- **Delete**
  - Deletes the selected clip or set of clips
- **Undock**
  - Moves the panel to its own window for more flexible window management
- **Views**
  - Switch between **Timeline, Playlist, Matrix*,**and **Videos*** views to see the edit in different presentations from the dropdown menu

> *****NOTE: These features are exclusive to Editor Max users.

### Hotkey To Flag Clips

Assigning a hotkey to flag clips can make the workflow simpler and help remove the need for excessive mouse clicks. To assign a hotkey, select the **Tools**menu, then **Options**. Under the Hotkeys tab, scroll down to Flag a Clip, click **Add**to input your desired key and click **Ok** to complete.

## Summary

With redesigned tools and added features, the MAX Editor 12 Timeline view is more versatile than ever. Utilize more detailed views and filters to focus on the exact data, plays, and information you need. Flag and mark clips to revisit later, use in Custom Edits, or easily toggle to Matrix view and compare the data in a robust and visually significant table. While Base Editor users can view Synergy Full Game Edits as a timeline, creating custom timelines is a unique feature for Editor Max users, providing new practice workflows and an opportunity to explore the data even further.

## MAX: Matrix View

### Overview

The Matrix view is a way to display all the tagged clips within your edit in a grid format. Within the Matrix view there are a number of ways to filter your information, allowing you to explore intersections of data to help you better view and sort your footage. From this view, you can play your selected clips as a temporary edit or add them to new or existing Custom Edits.

#### Getting Started

Once you have opened a Custom Edit or Timeline Edit, you can change the view to Matrix by selecting it from the drop-down menu in the top right of the panel. All of your tagged data will be displayed in the Matrix grid format.

![Screenshot: MAX: Matrix View](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565517-01.jpg)

In the top left of the Matrix panel, there is a slider to zoom in or out of the grid for easier viewing.

Above the grid you have drop-down menus to filter the displayed information, one for Rows, and one for Columns. These will help you refine your display to easily find and view your data.

You can sort your Rows and Columns by:

- **Players**
- **Play Calls**
- **Box Score**
- **Offense**
- **Play Types**
- **User Tags**
- **All**

Each column, row, and individual intersection are selectable. The number at the intersections indicates how many clips there are with that tag combination. To view the clips, double-click the intersection number, row, or column name, and a temporary edit will open and display the associated clips.

> **Note:**This temporary edit is similar to the temporary edit that is created when sending clips from the Team Site. You are able to manipulate the clips, move them to other edits or create new Custom Edits with them, but the temporary edit itself will not remain unless you save it using the carrot menu located in the edit's tab.

## MAX: Sequencer View

### Overview

The Sequencer view lets you organize clips from a custom edit into groups of your choice, creating a highly curated and organized view for your clips. Working in Sequencer view allows you easily move clips among groups within your edit, that helps to visualize your edit in a structured and organized way.

### Getting Started

Once you have selected the Custom Edit from your list that you would like to sequence, change your view to Sequencer from the views dropdown. All of the clips from your custom edit will be displayed in one group titled Ungrouped. Each row represents a unique group of clips. You can create groups by clicking the **Add Slide** button, and using either the **Add Grouping Text Slide**which creates a group with a title slide of the group name or**Add Grouping Image Slide**which creates a group with an image slide you can import from your hard drive. You can add additional title or image slides wherever you like within your groups from here as well.

![Screenshot: MAX: Sequencer View](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565518-01.jpg)

When adding a Title Slide or Grouping Text Slide, a window will appear with the following options:

- **Title** - name your group, this will name the row of clips, and also be displayed in the opening title slide for the group
- **Notes** - additional notes will be displayed on the title slide below the groups title
- **Duration** - adjust the slider to set how long the title slide will appear within the group
- **Copies** - this allows you to create multiple groups with the same properties at one time

![Screenshot: MAX: Sequencer View](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565518-02.jpg)

When adding an Image Slide or a Grouping Image Slide, a window will appear with the following options:

- **Title** - name your group, this will name the row of clips, and also be displayed in the opening title slide for the group
- **Notes** - additional notes will be displayed on the title slide below the groups title
- **Image File** - use the triple dot box to the right of the field to select an image file from your hard drive to be viewed on the Image Slide
- **Duration** -adjust the slider to set how long the title slide will appear within the group

![Screenshot: MAX: Sequencer View](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565518-03.jpg)

To edit existing group properties in the Sequencer view, select the row and click the **pencil** icon from the Sequencer toolbar, or view and manage Grouping slides in the Playlist view.

Once your groups have been set, you can begin organizing your sequences by dragging and dropping clips into your desired groups. It is important to note that as you organize your clips, this is the order the will be displayed in playlist view as well. Clips can be added before or after any clip within a group.

> NOTE: If you drag a clip and drop it between two groups it will create a new group which you can later edit using the group editing pencil tool.

As with the Timeline view, you can flag rows by right-clicking the row and selecting **Flag**, or flag clips by selecting the clip and clicking the **Flag** button from the toolbar. You can also add additional tags to clips by right-clicking the clip and selecting **Add User Tags**, or **Open Hierarchy**.

Now that your edit has been organized into sequenced groups, you can view each group of clips by double-clicking the row title for your group.

## MAX: Tagging Templates

### Overview

Tagging is an essential part of utilizing the Synergy Editor to its fullest potential. Creating unique, custom data points by developing a dynamic tagging template provides you with a versatile product that is both functional and visually exciting. Create your own custom tagging template as simple or detailed as you like to meet your organization's needs, use a template previously created by a member of your staff, or utilize one of our Synergy Preset templates, all stored under the Templates tab to get you started tagging and breaking down your footage.

#### Creating a Tagging Template

To create a new tagging template, click the **+** button in the upper right of the app, or the bottom right of any open panel, and then select **New Tagging Template**from the menu. A new, blank tagging template will open in the upper right panel, featuring a blank canvas on the left and an editing panel on the right.

![Screenshot: MAX: Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565520-01.jpg)

#### Existing Tagging Templates

You can open existing template by selecting the **Templates** tab at the top of the application. A list of all templates previously created by your team will populate the upper right panel for you to select from. You can use the search bar to search for a template by name, and you can also use the filter tool to display templates by the selected creators.

![Screenshot: MAX: Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565520-02.jpg)

#### Synergy Preset Tagging Templates

Synergy is excited to offer three new preset tagging templates, with more to come in the future. These templates have been designed as an easy jump off point into creating your own custom tagging templates. We are currently featuring templates for Roster, Scrimmage, and Practice.

The preset templates are identifiable by the Synergy logo on the tag icon to the left of the title. As pictured below, in order to make changes to a Synergy Preset template, you must first duplicate the template, and save it with a name of your choice.

![Screenshot: MAX: Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565520-03.jpg)

###

#### Button Types

To create a button, select the button type from the top of the template. You can either draw your button on the canvas by clicking and dragging to create the button shape, or double-click on the canvas to create the default shape. All buttons can be resized at anytime while in Edit mode. There are four different basic button types:

- **Manual Clip**: Controlled manually by clicking once to start the clip, and a second time to stop the clip
- **Auto Clip**: Clips footage with a predetermined, customizable amount of lead and lag time
- **Label**: Applies the associated information to the previously selected Manual or Auto clip
- **Shell**: Used to contain multiple buttons that share mutual data. Buttons used from within a shell apply not only the individual button data but the overall shell data as well, creating an easy way to apply your commonly used information without having to add it separately to each clip

#### Tagging Library

The Tagging Library allows you to create the kinds of dynamic tags and data points you're looking for, using pre-defined, selectable options while also providing the level of customization needed to make each template uniquely your own.

Begin by ensuring you are in Editing mode by toggling the Edit button to blue at the top of your tagging template and opening the Properties | Style panel to the right by clicking the arrow icon.

Select the button you wish to add tags to, then click the **Set Tag** button from the Tags section in the panel to open the Tagging Library. You can also right click the button and select**Set Tags** to add User Tags or select **Set From Library** to launch the library menu.

![Screenshot: MAX: Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565520-04.jpg)

![Screenshot: MAX: Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565520-05.jpg)

Once in the library window, there are five available tabs where new tags can be created, and existing tags can be selected. This includes **Play Calls**, **Teams**, **Synergy****Site**, **Players**, and **User Tags**. You can use the search bar to easily locate an existing tag or scroll through the list to browse them. If your desired tag does not exist, you can create a new tag by entering the name of your tag in the search bar, then selecting the **ADD** button. The new tag will be added to your Tagging Library for future use.

![Screenshot: MAX: Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565520-06.jpg)

You can select as many tags as you would like to be associated with the selected button by clicking the checkbox next to each tag, and it will be listed in the right panel under **Selected**. To remove a selection, click the**X** next to the undesired selection. Additionally, if any Synergy Site tags are selected, a text box will appear next to the tag allowing you to nickname your button. This will display on your button in the tagging template. Once all selections have been made, click the **OK** button, and your selected tags will be assigned to the button.

![Screenshot: MAX: Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565520-07.jpg)

#### Linked Buttons

Under the Properties selection you can choose to link buttons together using the Links tool, to enable multiple responses to a single click. To link two buttons, select a button to launch from, and either select a button to link to from the dropdown menus in the properties panel, or click and drag from the launching button to the response button using one of the hotkey options below:

- **Activation Link** (Control+Option+click and drag) - Selecting the first button to start cutting a clip also selects a second button to start cutting a clip. Activation tags can also be used to add multiple tags to an existing clip
- **Deactivation Link** (Control+Shift+click and drag) - Selecting the first button to start cutting a clip also selects the second button to stop cutting a clip
- **Exclusive Link** (Control+click and drag) - Selecting either button to start cutting a clip also selects the other to stop cutting a clip.

> NOTE: Buttons cannot be linked in more than one type of link. New types of links will override existing links. Since Auto Clips and Labels do not require manual termination, they are only available for activation links. Shells are not linkable.

Customize the color or your buttons and canvas, font type and size, outlines of buttons, even add images to buttons using the options in the Style pallet.

###

#### Deleting a Tagging Template

To delete tagging templates from your list and the cloud, simply select the template you wish to delete, and click the **Trash** icon, or right-click the template and select **Delete** from the menu. F A pop-up confirmation message will appear. Click **Ok** to complete the deletion process.

> NOTE: Deleting a template will remove it from the cloud, and it will no longer be accessible to any member of your team.

## MAX: Synergy Preset Tagging Templates

### Overview

Synergy is excited to debut our Preset Tagging Templates. These templates have been designed to give you a quick and easy starting point for your tagging workflow, creating an easily customizable template to help save you time. To find the Synergy Preset Templates, select the Templates tab at the top of the app, and either search by name using the toolbar, or filter by Creator, selecting **Synergy**. The Preset templates are identifiable by the Synergy logo on the tag icon to the left of the template name.

![Screenshot: MAX: Synergy Preset Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565521-01.jpg)

> NOTE: Synergy Preset Templates must be duplicated in order to modify. Users cannot make changes to the original template.

####

![Screenshot: MAX: Synergy Preset Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565521-02.jpg)

#### Roster

The Roster template allows you to house your players information. Adding your players here allows you to use copy and paste to quickly add each players button to any other open template. This can help assure that your player tags stay the same across all templates, whether creating custom edits, printing box scores, or publishing to the Practice Tab on the Synergy Team Site. It is important to ensure when entering your players information that the name in the Player field is the way you would like it to be viewed wherever the data is output. You can use Nickname to change the display of the Player button without affecting the Player tag.

#### Scrimmage

The Scrimmage template is a starting point for tagging practice scrimmages or exhibition games. The template allows your to set two teams, and record boxscore events.

![Screenshot: MAX: Synergy Preset Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565521-03.jpg)

#### Practice

The practice template allows you to copy and paste your roster to it, and record boxscore events as they occur. This template also has a column of manual drill buttons, allowing you to name your drills, and run the manual clip for the length of each drill, for easier sorting of drill specific data for each of your players.

![Screenshot: MAX: Synergy Preset Tagging Templates](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565521-04.jpg)

## MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging

### Overview

> NOTE: This feature is exclusively available to Editor Max users.

###

### Creating a New Practice Timeline

To get started, you will need to a bring practice video into the Editor. This practice footage can either be live captured, or imported from previously recorded video.

####

#### Starting a Live Capture

To start a live capture, simply click the **New Live Capture** icon at the top right of the app, or click the **+** icon located at the top of the app, and in the bottom right of any open panel and select **New Live Capture**.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-01.jpg)

A window will appear giving you several options:

- Name your edit
- Change the file name
- Select event type
- Select your video input
- Include audio
- Push to the Synergy cloud
- Performance Mode (for slower connections)

Once you have made your selections, click **OK**.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-02.jpg)

#### Importing Video

To import previously recorded video, simply click the **Import Video** icon at the top right of the app, or click the **+** icon located at the top of the app, and in the bottom right of any open panel and select **Import Video**.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-03.jpg)

A window will appear giving you several option:

- Select your file(s)
- Change the date
- Select event type
- Change the edit name
- Express (files only accessible locally on your device, not uploaded to the cloud)
- Push to the Synergy cloud
- Include audio

Once you have made your selections, click **OK**.

Now that your video has been brought into the Editor, a new untagged timeline will appear in the bottom panel. If you have imported more that one video file, you can use the **Videos** view in the dropdown located in the upper right corner of your timeline, to arrange the order of the video files within your timeline. Simply click and drag to arrange the files in the order you desire.

If you chose to push your timeline to the cloud, a blue line appears above the timeline, indicating your timeline is available to your entire organization via the Synergy Editor. If the line is green, the timeline is only available locally on your device. In order for other members of your team to be able to access, it must be uploaded to the cloud, by selecting the video asset under the **Videos** tab, and clicking the **Upload to Cloud** icon.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-04.jpg)

### Tagging Your Practice

Once you have your timeline arranged to your liking, and pushed to the cloud if desired, it's time to start adding tags. Begin by clicking the **Templates** tab in the top right of the app, and opening a tagging template, whether using a Preset Synergy template, a saved template previously created by you or a member of your staff, or a creating a new blank template by clicking the **+** icon and selecting **New Tagging Template**.

> NOTE: Use the search bar and filters to easily locate Synergy templates, and existing saved templates.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-05.jpg)

You can make changes to the buttons in any template by selecting the **Edit** mode toggle in the top right of the template panel. While in edit mode, select the button you want to modify, and you can set a nickname for the button, assign players, change, add or remove tags, assign or change hotkeys, link tags, set button colors and many other options to help streamline your tagging workflow.

> Note: When making changes to a pre-existing template, make sure to duplicate and rename so the original template remains unchanged.

Once your template is built, it's time to start tagging your practice. Switch your template to tagging mode by clicking the **Edit** toggle, and then clicking the **Play** icon in the video window to begin viewing your practice film.

> NOTE: Only outcome stats from the tagging hierarchy will post to the Box Score and Team Site, user tags are not viewable at this time.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-06.jpg)

To create clips on your timeline, you can either click the button you want, or use the assigned hotkeys. As you tag your video, the clips will appear on the timeline to show where the tag fits within the video. You are able to pause, rewind, and flag your clips to edit your work as you move through the practice film. You can also switch between different views like Playlist, and Matrix to visualize and organize the data in different formats.

### Printing a Practice Box Score

Synergy Basketball users can print a box score of their tagged data directly from the Editor. Click the **carrot icon** of the desired timeline, select **Print**, then **Box Score**. This gives you easy access to a physical output of your user tagged data to share with your team.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-07.jpg)

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-08.jpg)

###

### Publishing a Practice To Team Site

Synergy Basketball users also have the ability to publish their user generated statistics of a practice to the new Practice Tab on the Synergy Team Site, allowing you to see your practice data alongside your game information in one secure place.

> NOTE: All information in the Practice Tab is only viewable by you and your team.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-09.jpg)

Click the **carrot icon** on your timeline tab, select **Team Site**, then **Publish**. Your practice data will then be viewable on the Synergy Team Site for only the members of your team. To remove a practice from the Team Site, open the timeline in the Editor, click the **carrot icon**, and select **Team Site**, then **Unpublish**. The timeline will still be available in the Editor, but will no longer be published on the Team Site.

![Screenshot: MAX: Setting Up Practice Tagging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565519-10.jpg)

> NOTE: Your timeline must be pushed to the cloud to be viewable on the Synergy Team Site.

For more information on the Team Site Practice tab, you can review the following article: Practice Tab (see the “Shot Charts and Practice” lesson in Synergy Team Site)

## MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis

This section will guide you through effectively using the Timeline feature in the Synergy Editor Max to segment your practice drills, analyze statistics and video, and share your insights with your team.

#####

#### **Understanding Timelines and Segments**

- Timelines**:** In the Synergy Editor Max, a practice Timeline represents a complete practice session.
- Segments: Segments allow you to divide your practice Timeline into different drill types. This segmentation is crucial for analyzing stats and video, specifically for each drill type, without the clutter of other drills.

####

#### **Creating and Managing Segments**

Segments are powerful tools for focused analysis.

#####

##### Creating a New Segment:

Select a spot on the Timeline where you want a new segment to begin, then click the **Add Timeline Segment** button.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-01.jpg)

This action will open the Timeline Segment Library.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-02.jpg)

You can use the search bar to find an existing segment type. Alternatively, click the **ADD** button to create a new segment title. You can also choose a color to associate with your segment title.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-03.jpg)

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-04.jpg)

A new segment will be created, starting from your selected point and extending to the end of the timeline or until the next segment line. You can then drag the in and out points of the segment to precisely define the desired time range for that segment.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-05.jpg)

#####

##### Using the Segment Filter:

- To focus on a particular segment type, use the **Segment Filter**.
- When a segment is filtered, only clips within that selected segment type will be displayed.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-06.jpg)

####

#### **Analyzing Segments**

##### Box Score for Segments: With a single segment filtered, you can view or print a box score specifically for that segment, providing a clean view of the drill's performance without other practice data.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-07.jpg)

The following pop-up will display, informing you that the Timeline has a Segment Filter applied, and will limit the data displayed.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-08.jpg)

The box score of just the specified segment will then be displayed, and is available to print.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-09.jpg)

#### **Creating Custom Edits from Segments:**

Filter for a single segment, then select all the rows (clips) within that segment.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-10.jpg)

Right-click and choose **Create a Custom Edit** from the menu. This will create a new Custom Edit containing only the clips from your selected segment.

#####

#### **Publishing Timelines to the Synergy Team Site**

Publishing your segmented Timelines to the Team Site allows for broader team access and more refined analysis.

#####

##### How to Publish:

Click the hamburger menu (three horizontal lines) for the Timeline you wish to publish. From the dropdown menu, select **Team Site**, then **Publish.**This action publishes the entire Timeline to the Synergy Team Site.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-11.jpg)

#### **Viewing Published Timelines on the Team Site:**

Once published, you can filter all your practices on the Team Site by **Segment title** (drill type). Use the **Segment Dropdown Menu** on the Team Site, which will list all segment titles from your published practices.

![Screenshot: MAX: Using Timelines and Segments for Practice Analysis](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000587235-12.jpg)

Select the segment (drill type) you want to review. The Team Site will then display *only* those segmented clips across *all* your published practices, offering a highly refined view of player performance in specific scenarios over multiple practices.

#### **Important Considerations for Team Site Display:**

For a clip to be displayed on the Team Site, it **must have a player tagged and a stat associated with it.**

If you make any adjustments to your Timeline *after* it has been published to the Team Site, you **must publish it again** for those changes to be visible on the Team Site.

modules.content:
## Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor

Shot charts are now viewable for Synergy tagged games within the Synergy Editor. When you select a clip attached to a shot, the shot location will highlight on the shot chart. The shot chart can be displayed by clicking the gray triangle to the right of your edit from the Timeline, Playlist, or Sequencer view.

![Screenshot: Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000576098-01.gif)

Shot charts can also be placed on Tagging Templates for adding plot points to practice clips.

To add a shot chart to your template, create a new tagging template, or open an existing template. You can then, while in Edit mode, draw a shot chart on your template by selecting the **Draw Shot Chart** button, which is next to the Shell button above the tagging template canvas.

![Screenshot: Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000576098-02.jpg)

Once selected, choose between **NBA**, **College**, **WNBA/FIBA**, or **High School**. Then, click and drag on the canvas to create the shot chart the size you would like, and position it where you would like.

![Screenshot: Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000576098-03.gif)

Once created, while tagging your practice, the chart behaves similar to a label. When recording a shot event, tag your event as you normally would, you can then mark the event location on the shot chart. For example, a 3 point FG shot is missed, you would click the 3 FG Miss tag, then click the event location on the shot chart within your template.

![Screenshot: Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000576098-04.gif)

The shot location is now associated with your tag, and will display when that clip is selected. Plot points on the shot chart will appear in red for made field goals, blue for missed, or gray when not attached to shots.

![Screenshot: Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000576098-05.jpg)

With your both your edit and template open, when you select a clip associated with a shot, the location will highlight on the shot chart attached to the edit, as well as display in the shot chart within your tagging template.

![Screenshot: Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000576098-06.jpg)

Additionally, when you double click a plot point on the shot chart, the associated clip will play in the video player.

![Screenshot: Shot Chart Viewing and Tagging in the Synergy Editor](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000576098-07.gif)

## Overlay Features

#### **Overview**

These tools allow for dynamic annotations and visual aids directly on your video content, making your insights clearer and more impactful.

#### **Overlay Menu**

To begin utilizing these features, simply click the **Show Overlay Menu** button. This button is positioned in the bottom left corner of the Video Player panel.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-01.jpg)

Once the Overlay Menu is active, you will discover a variety of tools, each crafted to serve a specific purpose in your video annotation workflow.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-02.jpg)

#### **Text**

The Text feature enables you to add a custom text box directly onto your video. To create a text box, simply click and drag. Once created, you can type in your desired text, reshape the box to an appropriate size, and drag it to its optimal location on the screen.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-03.jpg)

The Properties menu offers extensive customization options for your text, allowing you to adjust the font, size, and orientation. You can also refine the visual appearance by changing the outline color, fill color, opacity, or the text color itself, ensuring your messages are presented clearly and effectively.

####

#### **Play Diagramming Tools**

These specialized tools are indispensable for diagramming plays, illustrating movements, and providing clear visual explanations directly on your video.

Cut Line Tool

To use the Cut line tool, first select the tool, then click on the video to mark the starting point of your line, and finally drag to its desired end point. While lines are initially straight, they can be effortlessly transformed into curves by selecting the red dot located in the middle of the line and dragging it in the direction you wish the line to bend. If you would like to return to a straight line, double-click the red dot in the center.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-04.jpg)

For situations requiring an angle rather than a smooth curve, a simple right-click on the line, and select **Properties** from the dropdown menu. Here you can switch the line type from curved to angled. Furthermore, this properties menu allows for detailed customization of the line type, color, and thickness, ensuring your diagrams are both accurate and aesthetically pleasing.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-05.jpg)

#### Complementary Line Tools

In addition to the Cut Line Tool, the **Screen Line, Pass Line,**and**Handoff Line**tools are also available. These tools operate with the same intuitive functionality as the Cut Line Tool, providing a consistent and efficient experience for various diagramming needs. These are all visually customizable in the properties menu,

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-06.jpg)

#### **Line Tool: Simple Divisional Lines**

For straightforward divisional needs, the Line Tool allows you to draw a simple straight line. This is particularly useful for segmenting the court or screen into distinct areas, aiding in spatial analysis.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-07.jpg)

#### **Shape Tools**

The shape tools provide the ability to draw circles and rectangles on your video, to highlight specific areas. Select a shape from the toolbar, click and drag the shape on the video, then utilize the various points to stretch and adjust the shape to your desired proportions.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-08.jpg)

The Properties menu offers comprehensive customization for these shapes, including adjustments to the outline thickness and color, line type, fill color, and opacity. This ensures that your highlighted areas are both precise and visually distinct.

#### **Spotlight Tool**

The Spotlight Tool is an excellent feature for drawing immediate attention to a particular player or area within your video. By clicking and dragging, you can create the base of the spotlight around your target, which will then project a conical spotlight from above.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-09.jpg)

Should you prefer a less dramatic effect, the properties menu allows you to remove the cone, leaving just an oval spotlight. Additionally, you can adjust the fill color and opacity of the spotlight.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-10.jpg)

####

#### **Images**

The Images tool offers the flexibility to incorporate external images from your device directly into your video. To add an image, simply click the Image tool, select your desired file, and it will appear on your video. Once placed, you can easily adjust its size and position by clicking and dragging, seamlessly integrating external visual content into your analysis.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-11.jpg)

#### **Stickers**

Stickers offer a quick and efficient method for adding helpful imagery to your video. This collection includes visual markers such as Player Numbers (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), tactical indicators X1-X5, and common sports equipment representations including circles, balls, and cones.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-12.jpg)

You have full control over their presentation; their size can be easily adjusted by clicking and dragging, and their outline color can be customized through the dedicated properties menu to match your specific visual requirements.

####

#### **Customizing Your Overlay Toolbar**

The overlay toolbar is customizable, allowing you to tailor it to your individual preferences and workflow. By right-clicking on any tool, you gain access to options that enable you to rename it, remove it from the toolbar, or set its default properties. This ensures that each time you access a tool, it will be configured precisely to your liking.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-13.jpg)

You can also add to your toolbar by clicking the **Add Overlay Tool Button** located on the right, selecting from a list of available tools to add. Additionally, you have the ability to create multiple instances of the same tool on your toolbar, each with its own distinct set of saved customizations, significantly enhancing efficiency for varied analytical tasks.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-14.jpg)

#### **Telestration**

Live telestration transforms your video player into a temporary chalkboard, offering an immediate and intuitive way to annotate during playback. When the Overlay menu is closed, you can simply click and hold your cursor over the screen at any point. This action will instantly pause the video, allowing you to draw directly on the screen. These spontaneous drawings are temporary, disappearing after a few seconds as video playback resumes. This dynamic feature is available for use whether you are reviewing individual clips or entire timelines, providing a fluid and responsive annotation experience.

![Screenshot: Overlay Features](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565514-15.jpg)
