modules.content:
## Creating a Custom Edit

### Overview

Custom edits are unique video playlists that can be exported or shared with staff members and players. With a variety of innovative tools, create your own curated video playlist with clips from the Synergy Team Site, or import your own video to trim and use. This guide explains how to create, open, and customize your workspace view when working with custom edits.

### Create Custom Edit

Create a Custom Edit at any point in the editing process. To create a Custom Edit, click on the **+** icon in the top right of the Editor or in the lower right corner of any open panel.

![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-01.jpg)

When prompted, give your new Custom Edit a distinct name and click **OK**. Use only letters and numbers, no symbols. You will see the new Custom Edit appear in the Custom Edits list. You can create as many Custom Edits as you need.

**
![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-02.jpg)**

####

#### Duplicating a Custom Edit

This feature allows you to copy an existing custom edit. You can use this to create scouting templates that can be easily duplicated, create a unique version of an edit you'd like to share, make changes to an edit someone has shared with you, or for a variety of other reasons. To duplicate an edit, under the Custom Edits tab, simply right-click on the edit you wish, and select **Duplicate**from the menu. If the edit is open, you may also click the **carrot icon**, and select **Duplicate**. Your duplicated edit will appear at the top of your Custom Edits list with "Copy" in the title to indicate that it is a duplicated edit.

![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-03.jpg)
![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-04.jpg)

### Working with Custom Edits

#### Open a Custom Edit

Select the edit you want to work with, then select one of the four destination options. You can choose from **Open Top Left**, **Open Top Right**, **Open Bottom** **Left**, or**Open Bottom Right.**You can also right-click on the edit, select **Open**, then select which panel to open it in. Double-clicking on an edit title will open it in the top right panel.

![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-05.jpg)
![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-06.jpg)

One of the benefits of the Editor 11 is being able to work with multiple edits, or have multiple views of the same edit open simultaneously. When you have custom edits open in multiple destinations, it will look similar to this: 1) Open top left, 2) Open top right, 3) Open bottom left, and 4) Open bottom right.

> NOTE: Matrix and Sequencer views are exclusive to Editor Max users.

![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-07.jpg)

####

#### Close a Custom Edit

To close a custom edit, simply click the **carrot icon** on the edit tab in the panel you wish to close, and select **Close**.

![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-08.jpg)

#### Destination Edits

When working with multiple edits, it is important to make note of which edit is designated as the destination edit. This will be annotated by a blue line under the designated edit tab. By default, the first edit open is designated as the destination edit.

![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-09.jpg)

However, you can set any edit as the destination by selecting **Set as Destination** from the carrot menu of an edit's tab. This is of particular importance, especially when moving clips between multiple edits using hotkeys, or the **ADD+** button, as they will be added to the edit designated as the destination*.*

![Screenshot: Creating a Custom Edit](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565511-10.jpg)

#### Resize your View

Customize your workspace view by adjusting the height and width of any panel. Hover your mouse over any intersection of views or the Video Playback Panel. Once the double arrow icon is visible, drag to resize the view.

### Summary

Custom edits are at the very core of the Synergy Editor 11 experience. Understanding the basics of creating a Custom Edit is essential for creating unique, relevant playlists curated to your individual needs.

## MAX: Timeline Edits (Formerly Source Edits)

### Overview

With the Editor Max, not only can you download Timelines of full game video from the Synergy Team Site, you can also create your own unique Timelines from live captured or imported video. Timelines can be created from your video and tagged by you, using Synergy Preset Templates, or your own custom built tagging template. Integrating the Tagging Hierarchy in your tagging template allows you to easily and quickly make a comprehensive, customizable template to break down your footage. Your Timelines are accessible under the Timelines tab at the top of the Editor.

![Screenshot: MAX: Timeline Edits (Formerly Source Edits)](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565513-01.jpg)

### Features

Timelines allows you to view or create a chronological representation of the video along with all tagged information added by Synergy and your staff. Timelines offer many tools, customizations, and visualization of your data. Some features included with Timeline edits are:

- **Automatically share Timelines with your team:**
  - All Timelines created within the Editor are automatically shared with everyone on your team with Editor permissions for easy accessible review under the Timelines tab.
  - **Add Timeline clips to Custom Edits** using drag-and-drop or hotkey.
  - Add a clip, selection of clips, or entire rows to a Custom Edit by selecting the clip(s) or row in the Timeline, and then hotkey to your destination edit, or drag-and-drop to your desired edit.
  - Adding clips from your Timelines actually creates a copy of those clips, which can be trimmed and tagged in the new edit without changing your source data and durations.

**Add and arrange video within your Timeline:**

- For example, if you want to combine video for 2 or more player training sessions, or if you’ve captured a game using multiple media files, you can add and re-order the media files any way you choose using the **Videos** view.
- You can arrange the media files even if you’ve already created clips on the existing media in the Timeline edit. The Timeline view will adjust according to how you order new media.

- **Print a Boxscore:**
  - Easily print a boxscore of all tagged data within the timeline by clicking the **carrot icon** on the edit tab, and selecting **Print** > **Boxscore**.

![Screenshot: MAX: Timeline Edits (Formerly Source Edits)](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565513-02.jpg)

- **Publish user created Timelines to the Synergy Team Site:**
  - Whether tagging a practice or exhibition, you can securely publish your data to the Synergy Team Site where it is only visible to you and your team by clicking the **carrot icon** on the edit tab, then selecting **Team Site** > **Publish**.

![Screenshot: MAX: Timeline Edits (Formerly Source Edits)](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565513-03.jpg)

## Organizing Edits Using Folders

### Overview

Having an organized workspace is important. When working with playlists, the number of custom edits can grow quickly, making it difficult to locate the exact edit you're looking for. Editor 11/ Editor Max allows you to create unique folders to organize all of your edits and timelines in a simple view for easy reference and quick access.

### Creating a Folder

You can create a folder at any point in the editing process. To create a folder:

- Open the folders panel to the left of the Custom Edits tab by clicking the **arrow** icon to expand.
- Select or hover over the Custom Edits folder, and click the **+** icon to the right.
- Name your folder, and click **OK**. Your newly created folder will appear below in alphabetical order.
- To create sub-folders, select the parent folder, click the **+** icon, name your folder, and it will appear within the selected folder.

You can expand and collapse folders containing sub-folders with the arrow icon to the left of the folder name to view their contents.

> NOTE: You can also use right-click on an existing folder to create a sub-folder within it, or a create a new Custom Edit within the selected folder.

### Moving an Edit to a Folder

To move a Custom Edit or multiple custom edits from you list into a specific folder:

- Open the folders panel by clicking the **arrow** to access your folders.
- Select **Display all Custom Edits**at the bottom of the folder list.
- From your Custom Edits list, drag and drop an Edit or multiple custom edits into your desired folder.

### Delete a Folder or Custom Edit

To delete an unwanted folder or custom edit, right-click and select delete from right click menu, or left click once on the desired folder or edit to highlight it, then select the **Delete** icon from the toolbar. Click **Ok** to confirm.

### Adjusting The Folder Panel

To adjust the size of the folder panel, hover over the separation line until the cursor turns into a double arrow, and then move your cursor side to side to set your desired width.

####

### Searching Your Folders

The search bar located above your edit list provides a quick way to find a specific edit from your custom edits or timelines list. To search, begin by typing in the name of the edit. The search list is dynamic, so as you begin to type, results will be listed.

> **NOTE**: The search bar feature will only search within the folder that is selected. To search all edits, ensure **Display all Custom Edits** at the bottom of the folders list is selected.

### Summary

Folders can be used to organize and categorize your ever-growing list of Custom Edits and Timelines. Organizing your edits into folders for easy access and sharing is a simple process and allows you to work in a clutter-free space.

modules.content:
## Sharing Custom Edits

### Overview

The ability to share custom edits is a powerful tool. You can share a custom edit with your coaching staff within the Synergy Editor, or share an edit with a player to view with the in-browser video player, allowing for quick and easy review of your footage breakdown.

### Sharing a Custom Edit with Team Members In the Editor

Sharing your custom edit in Editor allows you to send a copy to any member of your organization who has access to the Synergy Editor. This simple process will send a copy of your custom edit directly to the desired users device, automatically populating under their Custom Edits tab.

You can either **right-click** on the title of the custom edit in your list, or, with the custom edit open, click the **carrot icon** on the edit tab at the bottom of the panel. Select **Share**, then **in Editor**.

This will bring up a window with a list of all of your team members with Editor permission. You can use the search bar at the top of the list for easy location, or scroll through the list alphabetically. Simply click the **+** icon next to the desired recipients name, and click **OK**. You can select as many recipients as you desire. Once you have clicked OK, the recipients will have a copy of your custom edit appear at the top of their list of Custom Edits in the Editor.

### Sharing a Custom Edit with Players

If the players you would like to share your custom edit with do not have Editor permissions, you can still share your edit with them by creating a URL.

You can either **right-click** on the title of the custom edit in your list, or, with the custom edit open, click the **carrot icon** on the edit tab at the bottom of the panel. Select **Share**, then **Create URL**.

This will generate a unique URL that can be copied and shared via email. The recipient(s) then only need to copy and paste the link into their browser, where they will be prompted to sign into Synergy, and the custom edit will play in the Synergy In Browser Player.

![Screenshot: Sharing Custom Edits](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565512-01.jpg)

## Edit Sharing and Collaboration

You can easily share Edits with your team—whether you're providing access for review or collaborating on video breakdowns.

####

#### How to Share an Edit

1. **Right-click** on the edit you want to share from the list of your edits, or click on the three-line hamburger menu in the upper left of the panel while the edit is open.
2. Select **Share** from the dropdown menu, then select **in Editor**.

####

![Screenshot: Edit Sharing and Collaboration](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583888-01.jpg)

#### In the window that appears, you’ll see a list of all users on your team. At the top, there are two tabs: **Viewers** and **Editors**.

####

![Screenshot: Edit Sharing and Collaboration](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583888-02.jpg)

#### Viewer Access

In the **Viewers** tab, select any team members who need **view-only access**. These users will be able to watch the Edit and see any updates made, but they won’t be able to make any changes to the edit.

####

#### Editor Access

In the **Editors** tab, choose the users you want to **collaborate** with. Editors can view and make changes to the Edit. Any updates they make will be visible to all users the Edit has been shared with.

####

When you have shared an edit, a filled in Share icon will be displayed to the right of the edit name, indicating you are the creator of this shared edit. When an edit has been shared with you, the outline of the Share Icon will be displayed.

####

![Screenshot: Edit Sharing and Collaboration](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583888-03.jpg)

#### Sharing with Groups

Creating a New Group:

1. Click the **Pick from** **Group** button underneath the search bar.
2. Select the **+**icon from the dropdown menu to create a new group.
3. You will then be prompted to provide a name for your new group.

![Screenshot: Edit Sharing and Collaboration](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583888-04.jpg)

Adding Users to a Group**:** To assign a user to an existing group:

1. Hover your cursor over their name in the user list.
2. Click the **Assign to Group**icon that appears to the right of their name.
3. Select the desired group from the subsequent dropdown menu.

![Screenshot: Edit Sharing and Collaboration](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583888-05.jpg)

Sharing with an Existing Group:

1. Click the**Pick from** **Group** button located underneath the search bar.
2. From the dropdown menu, select the specific group you wish to share the edit with. All members of that group will then be granted the appropriate permissions.

####

![Screenshot: Edit Sharing and Collaboration](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583888-06.jpg)

#### Managing Shared Access

All selected users will appear in the panel on the right, organized by **Viewers** and **Editors**. To remove access, simply click the **X** next to a user’s name, then confirm by clicking **OK**.

![Screenshot: Edit Sharing and Collaboration](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583888-07.jpg)

> Note: Older Timelines will still show as available for all team members, but new Timelines will be private by default. Access to older Timelines can be restricted now by the creator through this process.

#### Duplicating Shared Edits

When an edit has been shared with you, you may want to create your own personal copy to make changes without affecting other team members viewing the shared edit. This is especially useful if you have a Viewer role, which prevents you from making direct changes to the shared edit.

To create an independent copy:

1. **Right-click** on the shared edit's tab.
2. Select **Duplicate** from the menu.

This action creates a separate, modifiable copy of the edit, allowing you to make changes as needed without altering the original shared version.

![Screenshot: Edit Sharing and Collaboration](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583888-08.png)

Sharing Edits ensures your coaching staff and players are always aligned—whether reviewing strategy, analyzing performance, or preparing for the next game.

## Clip Messaging

Clip Messaging allows collaborators to communicate directly on individual clips within an edit, keeping feedback and discussions contextual and easy to follow.

#### **Sending a Clip Message**

In Playlist view, each clip has a message icon under the Chat column.

- Click the message icon to open the chat window for that clip.
- Type your message and click **Send** to post it.

####

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-01.jpg)

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-02.jpg)

#### **Message Status Indication**

The message icon reflects the status of messages on a clip:

- **Empty message bubble**: No messages exist for this clip.
![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-03.jpg)
- **Message bubble with lines**: Messages exist and have been read.
![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-04.jpg)
- **Filled message bubble**: There are unread messages on the clip.
![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-05.jpg)

#### **Chat Window**

When the chat window is open, an **Info** button appears to the left of the message entry field. Clicking **Info**displays:

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-06.jpg)

- The total number of users who have access to the edit.
- A dropdown list showing the names of those users.

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-07.jpg)

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-08.jpg)

Select **Change** to open the Share window, where you can add or remove users from the edit.

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-09.jpg)

#### **Modifying Messages**

When hovering over a message in the chat window, you can mark the message as unread, edit the message, or delete the message. If a message has been deleted, a notification will be displayed in the chat.

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-10.jpg)

#### **Visibility and Access**

Clip messages are visible to all users the edit has been shared with, including both **Viewers** and **Editors**. Messages always appear in the Chat column, regardless of user role.

**Note**:Clip messages do not transfer when a clip is copied. Messages remain associated with the original edit that was shared.

#### **Viewing All Conversations**

Click the **message icon** in the bottom-right corner of the app to view all conversations. Unread conversations are displayed first in a pop-up.

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-11.jpg)

Selecting a conversation will open the message panel, showing messages from newest to oldest. If there are no unread messages, clicking the message icon opens the message panel directly.

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-12.jpg)

#### **Jumping to a Clip from Messages**

Each message in the message panel will display a **Play** icon when hovered over. Click the Play icon to jump directly to the associated clip. The related edit will load in the lower panel, providing immediate context.

![Screenshot: Clip Messaging](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000592903-13.jpg)

modules.content:
## Save Edits for Offline Use

You can save any Edit for offline viewing, perfect for reviewing game footage or training content when you're away from a stable internet connection.

####

#### How to Save an Edit Offline

There are two ways to make an Edit available offline:

- **Right-click** on the Edit in your library, then select **Make Available Offline** from the dropdown menu.
- Or, **select** the Edit, and click the **Make Available Offline** icon in the top right corner (located next to the trash can icon).

####

![Screenshot: Save Edits for Offline Use](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583890-01.jpg)

#### Download Progress

After selecting **Make Available Offline**, a **progress bar** will appear next to the Edit name. This shows the caching status of the video.

Once caching is complete, you’ll see a **green dot with an arrow** in the **Offline** column. This means the Edit has been successfully saved and is now available for offline use.

####

![Screenshot: Save Edits for Offline Use](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583890-02.jpg)

#### Storage Considerations

- Offline Edits video caches are stored locally on your device and will take up disk space.
- These video cache files remain available until they are manually removed—you don’t need to worry about them being cleared automatically.

####

#### To Remove an Edit from Offline Storage

If you need to free up space:

- Right-click on the Edit.
- Select **Remove Offline** from the dropdown menu.

![Screenshot: Save Edits for Offline Use](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000583890-03.jpg)

This will allow the cached video of the Edit to be cleared but will not remove it from your library or affect your online access.

## Offline Workflow

### Overview

The ability to work in the Synergy Editor while offline is very helpful tool when you find yourself without an internet connection. With a small amount of preparation, you have the ability to continue your work offline, and have that work sync back up when you regain an internet connection.

### Ensure video has been cached

In order to ensure you can work with video while in offline mode in the Synergy Editor, you must ensure that all video files have been cached on your device. Video that is sent from the Synergy Team Site to the Synergy Editor, is cached on your device to optimize your video playback experience. This also allows you to view the video files while offline.

Locate the video on the Team Site that you would like to work with, whether it is a set of clips, or the Full Game Video. Click the blue link associated with the video and ensure you have Editor selected for Playback in the Video playback parameters pop up. You can name the edit if you would like, then click **OK** to send them to the Editor.

![Screenshot: Offline Workflow](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570746-01.jpg)

Once the playlist has been sent to the Editor, it will populate in the lower panel, and you will see the clip numbers change from grey to black, signifying that the clip has been cached. Once all of the clips have turned black, the playlist is cached on your device.

![Screenshot: Offline Workflow](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570746-02.jpg)

When caching a Timeline, from a Full Game Video for example, you can view the grey bar above the timeline, turn to blue as it caches. Once the entire bar has turned blue, the entire timeline has been cached on your device.

![Screenshot: Offline Workflow](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570746-03.jpg)

### Working Offline

When offline, the online status indicator in the bottom right corner, will turn grey, as opposed to green when you are online.

![Screenshot: Offline Workflow](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570746-04.jpg)

You can continue to make changes to all edits and clips, as long as they have been cached. This includes Creating New Custom Edits, adding clips to Edits, Tagging, adding Notes, Text Overlay, and trimming in/out points of clips, as well as adding slides to your Edits.

Once you regain an internet connection, and the Editor is online, indicated by the green bars in the bottom left of the window, all of the changes that have been made offline will sync with the cloud. The cloud icon next to the online indicator will turn white while uploading the changes to the cloud.

Once the cloud indicator has turned grey, all changes have been updated, and you can then share your edits just as you normally would.

![Screenshot: Offline Workflow](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570746-05.jpg)

### Managing Your Cached Clips

In order to prevent your device from running out of disk space, it is important to periodically clear your cached clips. When older files are cleared, clips you have not accessed since that time will not be playable again unless you are Online. This means, even if the have been removed from the cache, once accessed again online, the clips will be re-cached, and will again be available for offline playback. None of your Edits or clips will be deleted when the cache is cleared, only the supporting cached video is removed.

In the Options menu of the Synergy Editor, you can set how long to keep cached clips on your device before being automatically cleared. Choose from after one Week, one Month, six Months, or Never. Click **OK** to save your choice. You can also click the **Clear Cache Now**button to clear your whole cache immediately

![Screenshot: Offline Workflow](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000570746-06.jpg)

Click the link below to view our YouTube video on the Offline Workflow and Storage Tips for the Synergy Editor.

<https://youtu.be/Jw7OVIdmeYc?si=fHTk3rnRzlnl1g9Z>

## Exporting Video

### Overview

Sharing and exporting your work is a vital piece of the workflow with the Synergy Editor 11. In this article, we will explore how to export a Custom Edit from the Synergy Editor/Editor Max. In the past, exported edits were limited to the full clip and could not retain any of the extra work you put in to make them unique and relevant. With Editor 11, you can now preserve all of the trims, overlays, and more when exporting your edit.

### Getting Started

There are several ways to export an edit. Right-click on an edit from your Custom Edit list or Timelines and select **Export** from the menu, or click the carrot icon to the right of an open edit tab and select the **Export** option.

Once selected, the Export pop-up window opens. This window allows you to:

- Set the **Location** of where you'd like to download the edit
- **Name** the edit
- Export it as **Audio/Video Only** (selecting this option bring up several more options)
  - Media:
    - **Full Edit**, which exports the entire edit
    - **Selection Only**, which exports only the clips selected within the edit
  - Extras:
    - **Express**, a speedier option with less precise trimming, no text overlay, and no clip combining
    - **Precision Trim**, includes exact trimming of clips within the edit
      - **Include Text Overlay**
      - **Combine clips into single video file**, this feature is exclusive to Editor Max users
- Export it as a **Copy of Edit**, this option creates a local file that may be shared with other devices, meant to assist with offline workflows. The full event video is stored along with this file and may take longer to transfer between devices.

![Screenshot: Exporting Video](https://pregame-academy.vickerydigital.com/assets/synergy/77000565635-01.jpg)

Choose where to send your edit by clicking the **Change** button and selecting a folder on your computer. Use the radio buttons next to the other options to make further export selections.

Once you've made your selections, click **OK** to begin the process of downloading the edit. Once the download starts, a window will appear that shows the conversion progress.

Depending on the selection you made before exporting, you will have several files available for sharing or use outside of the Editor. If you are an Editor Max user and you export the single video file option, you will see a single .mp4.

Exporting and sharing your work offline is a vital part of your workflow. With the ability to preserve trims and overlay along with ease of use, exporting and sharing edits, Editor 11 offers a more comprehensive experience than ever before.
